transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bringing you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today. Um, I hope I'm in the right place for this. I guess I came in because... well, I've just been feeling kind of wound up lately? Actually, almost all the time, if I'm being completely honest. 

It's just like my body is constantly bracing for the next bad thing to happen. And it happens even when everything is totally fine, like when I'm just sitting at my desk at work, or even when I'm out trying to enjoy dance night. I know it probably sounds a bit silly, and I really don't want to waste your time if it's just normal stress, but... does that make sense? Is that the kind of thing you can help with?

Can you tell me more about when these feelings of being wound up happen? Do they occur in specific situations, like when you're around other people, or does it seem to happen all the time, even when you're alone?

Um, it's pretty much all the time, honestly. Not just around people. I mean, it started out mostly about my condo, just worrying about repairs and things like that, which I know is normal, right? Everyone worries about their home. But lately, it's... well, it doesn't stay on the condo anymore. 

It just kind of jumps around? Like, I'll be by myself and suddenly I'm stressing over whether my cousin is secretly upset with me about something I said. Or I'll be at work—I do computer support—and I'll get terrified that I'm going to make a huge mistake on a call. And then it spirals into worrying about how I'll ever save enough money or just... move forward with my life in general. I'm sorry, I know I'm probably overthinking things that everyone deals with. Am I making a big deal out of nothing?
Do you notice any physical symptoms, like a racing heart, sweating, or stomach discomfort, when these worries come up?

Um, no, I haven't really noticed anything like that, to be honest. My heart doesn't really race, and I don't think I get sweaty or sick to my stomach or anything. It's mostly just... all in my head, I guess? 

I mean, I hope I'm explaining this right. I really don't want to make it sound like some huge medical emergency, because physically I think I'm mostly fine. I'm sorry if that's not very helpful. Is it okay if I don't have those symptoms? Like, is it normal to just have the worrying part without all the physical stuff you mentioned?
Do you feel like you’re able to control these worries, or does it seem like they just pop up and take over your thoughts even when you’re trying not to think about them?

Um... I try really hard to control them, I promise I do. I don't want to sound like I'm just letting myself spiral or anything. But... yeah, they do kind of take over sometimes, even when I'm actively trying to stop them. 

Like, even when I logically tell myself that I've already checked a spreadsheet, or I know for a fact I just sent an email... the thoughts just sort of keep looping? And then one 'what if' turns into five more before I can finally pull myself back. I'm sorry, I hope that doesn't make me sound completely incompetent or like I can't handle my job. I really try my best to just focus and push past it. Is it bad that I can't just snap out of it when I want to?
Can you tell me if these worries tend to focus on different areas of your life, like work, relationships, or other everyday things, or if they usually stay focused on just one thing at a time?

Um, well, I think I might have actually mentioned this a little bit earlier, but... yeah, they do tend to focus on a lot of different things. Like I said, it kind of jumps around? 

It's not just one thing. It's my condo, and work, and my cousin, and money... just everyday things, really. Normal things to worry about, I think. I just... I guess I just worry about all of them at once sometimes. I hope I'm not repeating myself too much, I'm sorry. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. Is it helpful that I'm explaining it this way?
How often do these feelings of constant worry and being wound up happen? Are they something you experience on most days, and have they been going on for a while?

Um, well, it's definitely not every single second of the day, I promise. I don't want it to sound like I'm just a wreck all the time. But... yeah, I guess it is most days. 

As for how long... um, it's been a little while. I think maybe around nine months? It kind of started getting worse when... well, when the loan on my condo started moving toward foreclosure. I know that's a pretty normal thing to be stressed about, right? Anyone would be worried about losing their home. I just... I haven't really been able to shake it since then. I hope it's okay that I let it get to me for this long. Does that timeline make sense for what you're asking?
Do you find it hard to relax, even when you’re in a calm environment or trying to rest?

Um, well... I do try to relax, I really do. I know how important rest is. But... yeah, I guess it is pretty hard for me to just switch off, especially at night. 

I don't want to sound like I'm not taking care of myself, but most nights I'll get into bed completely exhausted, and... my brain just kind of keeps going. It's like it just starts replaying all the loan notices I got, or work tickets I need to close, or just... things I might have missed during the day. I try really hard to just breathe and ignore it, but sometimes it's 2 or 3 in the morning before I can finally drift off. And even then, when I wake up, I usually feel like I barely rested at all. I'm sorry, I know I should probably have better sleep hygiene or something. Is it normal to have this much trouble winding down?
Would you say that you feel anxious or worried most days, and that these worries often feel intense or hard to manage?

Um, well... I really do try to manage it, I promise. I don't want you to think I'm just letting myself spiral out of control or anything. But... yeah, I guess it does feel pretty hard to stop sometimes. Most days, actually.

It's just... even when I try to be logical about it, like when I tell myself I've already checked my budget spreadsheet or I know I sent that important email for work... the thoughts just kind of keep looping in my head. I try to shut it down, but one "what if" just turns into, like, five more before I can finally pull myself back. I really am trying to get better at catching myself when I do it, though. I know I shouldn't let my thoughts run away with me like that. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Do you often feel restless, like you can't sit still, or like you're constantly on edge?

Um, well... I really try to stay composed, especially at work. I don't want to be that person who's always fidgeting or making everyone else nervous. But... I guess, yeah, I do feel pretty on edge a lot of the time. 

It's like... I came in because I just feel wound up almost constantly. Even when I'm just sitting at my desk, or, you know, when I try to go out for dance night with my friends—which I really do try to enjoy!—it feels like my body is just... bracing for the next bad thing to happen. Like I'm physically tense, even when I'm trying to have fun or just do my job. I really hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is, I know everyone gets tense sometimes. Is it okay that I feel that way even when nothing is actually going wrong?
Do you often feel unusually tired or like you don't have much energy, even if you haven't been doing anything physically demanding?

Um, well... I try not to complain about being tired, because I know my job isn't exactly physical labor or anything. I'm just sitting at a computer all day doing support tickets, so I really shouldn't be exhausted, right? 

But... I guess, honestly, I do feel pretty drained a lot of the time. Even on weekends when I haven't done much, I just feel this heavy sort of tiredness. I try to push through it and keep up with everything, I really do. I don't want to seem lazy or like I'm just not trying hard enough. It's just... sometimes it feels like just getting through the day takes all the energy I have. I'm sorry, I hope that doesn't sound like I'm just making excuses. Do a lot of people feel that way?
